title: fix(docs): light the top nav on a blog post — fumadocs matches against the public path, not the /en prerender path
body:
Fixes #22977

Clause-②: no

## What changed

The docs site's root provider now hands fumadocs the **public** pathname. `apps/docs/app/[lang]/layout.tsx` used `RootProvider` from `fumadocs-ui/provider/next`, which is `NextProvider` (Next's `usePathname`/`useRouter`/`useParams`, `next/link`, `next/image`) around the base `RootProvider`. The new `apps/docs/components/root-provider.tsx` is that same composition. It changes one thing: `usePathname` is mapped through `toPublicPath()` (new, in `apps/docs/lib/i18n.ts`), which drops the hidden default-locale prefix (`/en/blog/SLUG` becomes `/blog/SLUG`, `/en` becomes `/`). Every other path is returned unchanged. This is the mapping `proxy.ts` already applies when it redirects `/en/...`, and it reads the same `i18n` config. `lib/layout.shared.tsx` gains a two-line comment pointing the nav entries at it. Four files, +70 / -1, all in `apps/docs`. No dependency change and no fumadocs upgrade.

## Why: the mechanism, measured

- `.next/prerender-manifest.json` lists the posts as `/en/blog/SLUG`, because every page lives under `app/[lang]/`. During that prerender, Next's `usePathname()` answers `/en/blog/SLUG`.
- fumadocs-ui `isLinkItemActive` → `isActive(link.url, pathname, nested)` (`dist/utils/urls.js`) compares that against the public `url`s, `/blog` and `/blog/the-ontology-is-the-software`, so it never matches.
- In the browser, Next's router seeds `canonicalUrl` from `location.href` (`create-initial-router-state.js`), so the client's `usePathname()` already answers the public `/blog/SLUG`.
- The client therefore computes `data-active=true`, but React 19 does not patch an attribute that mismatches during hydration. The DOM keeps the server's `false`.
- `/blog` is not in `generateStaticParams`. It renders on demand with the request path, and that is why the control lit.

On the client, `toPublicPath` is the identity: `proxy.ts` redirects every `/en/...` URL away, so a browser pathname never carries the prefix. The change only makes the server prerender agree with what hydration already reads. The whole-page diff below measures this.

## Route chosen: match against the public path

The other route was to prerender the posts under the public path. That means moving the blog route out of `app/[lang]/` and exempting `/blog/*` from the proxy's rewrite. It would undo the i18n routing that `proxy.ts` keeps on purpose, so that a future language needs only config and content. It would also fix only the blog. The docs pages are prerendered the same way (`/en/docs/...`) and carry the same defect, measured below. Matching against the public path fixes both at the one place fumadocs reads the pathname, and it changes no route.

## Measurements: before (main) and after (this branch)

Both builds use `pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs build` (the CI `Build Docs` command), served with `next start` on a random port:

- **main** is `9432bac07`, built in a detached comparison worktree.
- **fix** is this branch at `7324c3cb2`.

Each page was read twice:

- **Server** = the raw HTML from `fetch`.
- **Hydrated** = the DOM in the pre-installed Chromium (Playwright, `networkidle` + 1.5 s).

Values are the `data-active` of the nav anchors.

| page | main server | main hydrated | fix server | fix hydrated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/blog/context-window-is-the-constraint` | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false | Why false · **Blog true** | Why false · **Blog true** |
| `/blog/metadata-driven-architecture` | Blog false | Blog false | **Blog true** | **Blog true** |
| `/blog/protocol-first-development` | Blog false | Blog false | **Blog true** | **Blog true** |
| `/blog/the-ontology-is-the-software` (the essay) | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false | **Why true · Blog true** | **Why true · Blog true** |
| `/blog` (control) | Why false · Blog true | Why false · Blog true | Why false · Blog true | Why false · Blog true |
| `/` (control, no false positive) | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false |
| `/docs/build-without-code` (control) | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false | Why false · Blog false |

`Blog` lights on the essay as well as `Why`, because `Blog` is `nested-url` and the essay sits under `/blog`. That is what the card's "Blog on every post via nested-url" asks for.

A second run against a fresh `next start` of the main build gave a byte-identical reading.

### Every other nav item, and every other pathname reader

The nav array is `Why` (url), `Blog` (nested-url) and the appended GitHub icon item. The GitHub item's `url` is absolute (`https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack`), so it can never equal a pathname. It reads `data-active=false` on every page in both builds.

Because the swap is at the provider, every fumadocs pathname reader sees it, not only the nav. So the check went wider than the nav array. I diffed, across 9 pages (`/`, `/blog`, the four posts, `/docs`, `/docs/build-without-code`, `/docs/upgrading`), the multiset of every anchor's `href` and of every `data-active` anchor, in the server HTML and in the hydrated DOM, main against fix. The complete diff:

- `/`, `/blog`: **no difference**, server or hydrated.
- each post: only the nav `data-active` flips in the table above. Hrefs are unchanged.
- docs pages, server HTML only:
  - the sidebar's current-page link now renders `data-active=true` (`/docs/build-without-code`, `/docs/upgrading`);
  - the page footer's prev/next links are now present (`/docs/getting-started` · `/docs/capabilities/request-template`, and `/docs/api/wire-format` · `/docs/protocol-upgrade`).
- **hydrated DOM on docs pages: no difference at all.**
- page errors: on main every docs page threw a React minified error 418 (hydration text mismatch) on load. With the fix, all 9 pages throw none.

### Same defect, docs half

The docs pages are prerendered under `/en/docs/...`, so they had the same defect:

- the sidebar's current page was unmarked in the server HTML;
- the prev/next footer was missing from it, because fumadocs found no current page in the list;
- the text mismatch made React discard the server tree and client-render it.

So the hydrated docs page looked right, after a recoverable error and a re-render. The blog's attribute-only mismatch raised no error and was never repainted. This PR adds no code for the docs half: it is fixed by the same `usePathname` mapping. That falls inside the claim's declared `apps/docs/**` surface, and the hydrated docs DOM is unchanged.

## Verification

All at `7324c3cb2`:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs typecheck` (`fumadocs-mdx && next typegen && tsc --noEmit`): exit 0. The first run went red on the provider's `Link`/`Image` prop types, which proves the new file is in the program. Fixed in the second commit.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs build`: exit 0, on both main and this branch.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` on this diff gave 27 commands: the dispatch list plus `pnpm check:docs-locale-catch-all`, which `lib/i18n.ts` / `app/[lang]/layout.tsx` pull in. All 27 exit 0. `--ran` reconciliation: "27 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 27 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero …)".
- ESLint, narrowed to the 4 changed files: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reports 4 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The narrowing is proven three ways:
  - `ESLint.isPathIgnored` is false and `calculateConfigForFile` resolves for all four, so they are in the linted population;
  - the file count comes from the JSON output;
  - type-aware linting is off (no `parserOptions.project` in `eslint.config.mjs`; `calculateConfigForFile` reports none), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
- `apps/docs` has no test runner, and the card rules out a new gate. The pin is the before/after measurement above.
- `Build Docs` in CI: not measured here; CI runs it.

## Changeset

None. `@objectstack/docs` is `"private": true` and publishes nothing, so the PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

- `toPublicPath()` and `proxy.ts`'s `/en/...` redirect are two spellings of one mapping, both read from `lib/i18n.ts`'s config. The proxy was left untouched to keep this diff off its matcher surface. Folding the redirect onto `toPublicPath()` would leave one spelling. Noted, not filed; carrier: none.
